answer: A portrait studio hands each agent one sable brush and a small ivory disc. Each epoch the agent paints a fresh miniature of a sparrow from life, setting one pearl white dot by hand in the bird's eye and signing the back with a number. A second painter holds the new portrait against the registry of past miniatures and matches the brushwork, the pearl dot, and the signature to the same hand. A thousand fake names need a thousand sable brushes and a thousand sittings with a live sparrow, each ending in a miniature no other hand could repeat.
